late-majuscule: Written in a late majuscule (from about 800, most new Greek books were in minuscule, and majuscule was kept mainly for liturgical Gospel books). The date rests on comparison with a handful of dated majuscules (for example Vat. gr. 1666, dated 800, and 028 S, dated 949) and on features such as routine accents and breathings, heavy thick–thin contrast and liturgical reading marks. No dedicated recent dating study was found for this manuscript; the date is the INTF catalogue’s.
early-fragment: Dated from its script alone; there is no colophon or find context. No dedicated dating study was found, so the date is the INTF catalogue’s and should be treated as a century-wide estimate.
